items.title: Delhi SEM court grants bail to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke
items.summary: A Delhi court on Saturday granted bail to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. The order was passed by a court of the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM). Dipke's legal team confirmed the development. The Court has imposed certain conditions on him. Details are awaited. Dipke and All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora were detained by the Delhi Police on October 16 ahead of the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest at Connaught Place. Dipke was picked up near his residence while heading to the protest at Connaught Place while Bora was detained while she was marching from Mandi House. Notably, CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are already in judicial custody after they tried to enter Jantar Mantar area.

items.title: Alliance Air pays over ₹16 lakh to 33 passengers after consumer court issues NBW over flight cancellation
items.summary: Over two years after abruptly cancelling a Hyderabad–Mysore flight, Alliance Air has cleared more than ₹16 lakh in compensation to 33 passengers following the issuance of non-bailable warrants by a Hyderabad consumer commission [Radha Devi Mandhana vs M/s The Alliance Aviation Ltd]. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, Hyderabad, comprising President Vakkanti Narasimha Rao and Members P V T R Jawahar Babu and Suma Vala , terminated execution proceedings on October 14 after recording satisfaction of the decree. The Bench also recalled the non-bailable warrants (NBWs) previously issued against airline officials. The dispute arose from an incident on June 2, 2022, when a 33-member family group, including senior citizens and infants, arrived at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport to board a flight to Mysore. Less than three hours before departure, the airline sent an SMS notifying them of the flight's cancellation. Left stranded without assistance or refreshments, the passengers were offered alternate seats only for a few members of the group, which they could not take.
